title: Affineness descends to a finite stage of a limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $0\in I$ and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of schemes over $S_0$, where $S_0$, $X_0$, $Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$ to $S_i$ ($X_i=X_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, $Y_i=Y_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]) and $f:X\to Y$ its base change to $S$. If $f$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], then $f_i$ is affine for some $i\ge0$ (Stacks Limits, Lemma 01ZN).

source.place: Lemma Tag 01ZN (lemma-descend-affine-finite-presentation, line 1750), in Situation Tag 081D (situation-descent-property, line 1739); its proof (lines 1757-1770): a finite affine open covering $Y_0=\bigcup_jV_{j,0}$, $U_{j,i}=f_i^{-1}(V_{j,i})$, $U_j=\lim_iU_{j,i}$ (Lemma Tag 01YX), Lemma Tag 01Z6 (lemma-limit-affine, line 680) and Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01S8 (lemma-characterize-affine)

proof.text: Restrict to the directed upper tail J = {i | i₀ ≤ i}. The explicitly proved equivalence Jᵒᵖ ≌ Over(op i₀) identifies the base-change diagram Eᵢ = X₀ ×_{S₀} Sᵢ with baseChangeDiagram D (f₀ ≫ h). By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit], baseChangeCone is limiting, and whiskering through the equivalence preserves this property. Transitions are affine base changes. Their projections to X₀ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2) gives qcqs of every Eᵢ. The compatible maps Eᵢ → Y₀ are the first projections followed by f₀.

The projection S → S₀ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-cone-affine-projections-opens](1). Therefore its base change Y → Y₀ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1). The hypothesis says f : X → Y is affine. The composite X → Y₀ is consequently affine: preimages of affine opens are affine by applying [pqf-def-affine-morphism] twice. The equation f ≫ pr₁ = pr₁ ≫ f₀ follows from pullback.map_fst.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-affine] with fixed base T = Y₀, diagram E on Jᵒᵖ, its base-change limit cone, and structure maps pr₁ ≫ f₀. The qcqs hypotheses are those of step 1 and of Y₀, and the limit map is affine by step 2. Obtain j ∈ J such that Eⱼ → Y₀ is affine.

The projection gⱼ : Yⱼ → Y₀ is affine by base change of Sⱼ → S₀. Since fⱼ ≫ gⱼ = pr₁ ≫ f₀ is affine, fⱼ is affine (Mathlib IsAffineHom.comp_iff). For completeness, this cancellation follows from [pqf-lem-affine-local-target]: on each affine open V of Y₀, both gⱼ⁻¹(V) and (gⱼfⱼ)⁻¹(V) are affine, so the induced map between them is affine; these opens cover Yⱼ. Thus return j.val and j.property. The tail contains i₀ even if the schemes are empty, so no nonemptiness of any scheme or affine-cover member is needed.

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Limits 01ZN in Situation 081D (limits.tex lines 1739-1770) and kept; stmt_deps kept. Proof written in six steps following the Stacks proof: (1) the base changes $X_T,Y_T,f_T$ for $T=S_i$ or $S$, $\mathrm{pr}_1:Y_T\to Y_0$ affine, $f_T$ the base change of $f_0$ over $Y_0$ (pasting) and quasi-compact and quasi-separated; (2) the finite affine covering $V_{j,0}$ of $Y_0$, the pieces $V_{j,T}$ (affine, covering) and $U_{j,T}=\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(U_{j,0})$, quasi-compact and quasi-separated (needed for Lemma 01Z6, which the source does not check); (3) $U_j$ affine ($V_j$ is affine because $p_0$ is affine, which the source leaves implicit); (4) $U_j=\lim U_{j,i}$ with affine transition maps, from Limits 01YZ (the $X_i$ have limit $X$) and 01YX(2) (preimages of an open), which the source cites as 01YX alone; (5) Limits 01Z6 for each $j$; (6) common index by directedness and Morphisms 01S8. No new node: every step uses existing nodes. All tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (01ZN, 081D, 01YX, 01YZ, 01Z6, 086P, 01S8).
